verdicts.reason: A keeps a clean text hierarchy and the original reading order (eyebrow, headline, subhead, CTA). But the leaf imagery shrinks to a small thumbnail crop, and the jar and the Lumen & Fig logo are tiny, stacked in an ad-hoc right strip, so the brand is barely visible; the legal block also takes a large share of the canvas. B keeps the leaf panel, but the headline crowds or abuts the leaf image. It also moves 'CLINICALLY TESTED' below the subhead, which breaks the reading order. The legal copy is shrunk to illegible size, and the jar and logo are tiny and crammed into the bottom-left corner.
